purpose: Everything needed to rebuild the MESHWEAVE POC environment on a different set of hosts.

ssh.note: Aliases live in ~/.ssh/config. Public key must be authorised on each new instance.

/root/models/phi-mini-moe-Q8_0.gguf.used_for: Phase 4/4.1 capacity claim; cannot be GPU-resident on any GPU

llama_cpp.clone_and_build: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp && cd llama.cpp && cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=75 -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF && cmake --build build --target llama-cli llama-server llama-tokenize ggml-rpc-server -j 8
llama_cpp.gpu_arches: 75 covers all three cards (Turing: 1660S 7.5, Quadro RTX 4000 7.5, 2070S 7.5)
llama_cpp.note: GGML_RPC=ON is required for ggml-rpc-server; the default target does not build it.

ports.note: Vast maps only ports requested at rent time. 10100 and 10200 are free on all three instances and are what the pipeline uses.

repo_remote: none - the repository is local to this machine; archive at ~/Downloads/meshweave-backups/
resume_checklist: 2. Add ~/.ssh/config aliases meshweave-host-a/b/c with the new IPs and ports
3. Rebuild llama.cpp per llama_cpp.clone_and_build (GGML_RPC=ON is essential)
4. Download both GGUF files and verify SHA-256 against this manifest
6. Re-run network benchmark: uv run python -m experiments.network.exp_net_002 (the pipeline assumes ~310 ms WAN RTT and 0.5 ms A-C)
7. Restart the chain and verify with docs/PHASE_3B_THREE_HOST_DISTRIBUTED_INFERENCE.md
8. If link characteristics changed materially, re-derive the partition: the 11/10/11 split assumed measured VRAM
